title: 9. Prime Minister – Special Safeguards (VERY FREQUENTLY ASKED)

blocks.content: The Special Protection Group provides proximate security to the Prime Minister of India and immediate family members residing with them at the official residence.

rows: 10 years automatically, extended based on annual threat assessment
Restricted strictly to 5 years from the date of leaving office
Provided to immediate family members regardless of residence
Provided only if residing at the official residence allocated to the PM/Former PM

items: Birbal Nath Committee recommended the creation of the Special Protection Group (SPG) in 1985.
Under the 2019 Amendment, former Prime Ministers receive SPG protection strictly for 5 years after demitting office.
Constitutional duties of the Prime Minister to furnish information to the President are laid down under Article 78.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Special Protection Group (SPG) was constituted in 1985 following the Birbal Nath Committee recommendations and statutory status was granted in 1988.
SPG provides proximate security to the Prime Minister of India and immediate family members residing at the official residence.
The SPG (Amendment) Act 2019 limits SPG security cover for former Prime Ministers and their families to a period of 5 years from leaving office.
Constitutional safeguards and duties of the Prime Minister regarding communication with the President are governed under Article 78.
